const r=`# TokenEconomizer 0.1.0 isolated repair

4 November 2026 IST · Windows PowerShell 7 · Python 3.14.8

## Baseline and reproduction

The candidate is a local clone without shared object hardlinks at revision \`85a8247bf4fc276a6f681446c359d7ca021b83b9\`. The original source clone was clean on \`main\`, with no repository or parent AGENTS.md found. The installed plugin manifest reported 0.1.0. The audit and local settings established that the plugin is enabled, shadow is false, global tool pruning is auto, and the EOD repository overrides tool pruning to propose. Codex CLI 0.166.0 is supplied environment information. The audit and verification did not launch it.

The original source reproduces the output discrepancy from the prior audit. The corrected reader also matched the retained one-file sample and combined the two disjoint retained segments of a second session. These spot checks used existing files read-only and exported no prompts, tool content, or session paths.

| Synthetic fixture | Original | Corrected |
|---|---:|---:|
| Audit counters, reported output | 62,679 | 49,751 |
| Audit counters, separately reported reasoning | 12,928 | 12,928 |
| Audit counters, weighted equivalents | 1,449,059 | 1,371,491 |
| Inherited baseline and repeat, fresh input | 235 | 35 |
| Inherited baseline and repeat, counted requests | 3 | 2 |
| Valid no-reasoning fixture, weighted equivalents | 54.25 | 54.25 |

The effective difference is 77,568 at the existing fallback output weight of 6. Cache reads and writes are subtracted from grand input when deriving fresh input. The ledger retains raw component fields and a separate effective estimate. Pricing weights were preserved.

## Folding and data quality

The six historical audit failures had zero matching retained rollout filenames in the inspected active and archived directories. The two unreadable folds had no saved transcript path. The four no-usage rows recorded zero prompts, but their original files are absent at the recorded paths. Their original parse or access outcomes cannot be reconstructed. Synthetic fixtures reproduced the old fold's inability to recover a moved transcript and its conflation of absent, invalid, inaccessible, and unsupported inputs.

The candidate searches for the same UUID in active and archived rollouts. It accounts for disjoint segments, coalesces exact timestamped usage copies, and leaves ambiguous overlap unpriced. It uses explicit per-call counters, bounded cumulative deltas and evidenced resets. Repeated cumulative snapshots do not count as requests. Cumulative-only opening balances, irreconcilable counters and incomplete required fields leave usage explicitly incomplete and effective usage null. Missing files, access failures, invalid rollout text, unsupported formats and readable rollouts without usage get separate statuses. The fold stores the usage status and reasoning field while preserving the existing once-per-session lock and fold identity.

## Offline verification

- Baseline against the new regression file — 17 expected failures and 1 pass. The pass covers previously valid accounting.
- Candidate — 22 passed, including 18 new regression cases and 4 focused existing cases. Coverage includes reasoning, cache reads and writes, per-call and cumulative counters, duplicate snapshots, inherited counters, resets, incomplete data, disjoint segments and ambiguous overlap, archival recovery, and persisted missing/no-usage results.
- The final test runs disabled pytest plugin autoload and caching, used isolated temporary paths, and blocked Python subprocess and network audit events during pytest. Baseline source was read from local Git before that guard. No dependencies were installed.
- \`git diff --check\` and reverse patch apply check passed. The patch SHA-256 is \`85F5960D46D30368CECD08ADB822E5C59E5021D5F5219BFB74AD9B173798E75C\`.

A future promotion should start with code review and an independent apply to a clean isolated checkout at the pinned revision. Use \`git apply --check repair.patch\`, then apply and rerun the focused tests. Verify hook delivery and ledger display in a disposable profile before approving any live change. Preserve the installed version and back up plugin state before a separately authorized promotion. Historical ledger rows require a separately reviewed migration, if any. To roll back this isolated candidate, reverse the patch in the candidate after \`git apply --reverse --check repair.patch\`, or discard the isolated checkout after retaining the evidence. There is no production rollback to perform.

## Proposed A/B benchmark — unexecuted

First replay identical sanitized fixtures against the pinned baseline and candidate offline. Require exact component accounting and explicit incomplete outcomes. For a separately authorized live pilot, use paired disposable Codex profiles with identical task, revision, model, effort, tool definitions, hook settings and data. Randomize run order and balance cold and warm cache. Compare raw usage, independently recalculated weighted equivalents, fold completeness, duplicate or lost events, side-call overhead and accepted task outcomes. Set a run and spend cap first. The accounting correction changes reported usage. Estimating real optimization savings would require a separate plugin-off control and matching task quality.

## Closeout

- **Status** — **TESTED / HOLD FOR REVIEW**. Focused checks passed. No installation, promotion, live-model calls, or paid benchmarks.
- **Risks** — The unavailable historical transcripts remain unresolved. Ambiguous or unsupported records intentionally remain unpriced, including overlapping segments without exact copy evidence. The existing once-per-session policy does not revise rows for later resumes. No old ledger was refolded. Codex exec side-call and experimental-harness schemas were outside the confirmed rollout defect and were left unchanged. Live Desktop and CLI hooks were not exercised.
- **Files changed** — Only in the isolated candidate, \`tokeneconomizer/trace/codex.py\`, \`tokeneconomizer/plugin/fold.py\`, \`tests/test_live_core.py\`, and \`tests/test_codex_accounting.py\`. The original clone remained clean and production Git status remained at 50 modified and 28 untracked entries. No installed plugin, production project, configuration or existing session records were edited by the repair.
- **Next steps** — Review the exact patch and decide whether to authorize a disposable-profile verification before considering promotion.
`;

# TokenEconomizer

A plugin for Claude Code, Codex, the Copilot CLI and Pi that reads finished sessions and changes
what later sessions in the same repository pay for: micro-skills, tool pruning, and a loop guard.
See `README.md` for the overview and the method, `docs/PLUGIN.md` for the design and the verified
agent behavior, and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for how the package fits together.

## Layout
- `tokeneconomizer/` — the one Python package, standard library only
  - `microskills/` — learn repository facts from finished sessions; render the injected block
  - `toolprune/` — unused-tool evidence and the deny-list proposal; Codex capability packages
  - `loopguard/` — the per-call failure-loop guard and its per-repository envelope
  - `trace/` — each agent's session-log format (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Pi, opencode)
  - `plugin/` — the runtime: hook dispatch, per-repository state, settings, the `te` CLI
  - `config.py`, `ledger.py`, `pricing.py`, `domain.py`, `stage.py` — shared by all three
- `plugin/` — the installable plugin directory: manifests per agent, hook files, launchers
  (`scripts/te`, `scripts/te-hook`), slash commands (`slash-commands/`, named in the Claude Code
  and Copilot manifests, since Codex would turn a `commands/` folder into duplicate skills), Codex
  skills (`codex-skills/`, Codex having no plugin slash commands), the Pi extension; `lib/` links
  the package
- `experiments/` — benchmark-only: `te_bench/` (adapters, arms, facade, benchmark-only
  controllers), `te_harness/` (Docker runners), `scripts/`, `workloads/`, its own `tests/`;
  its `README.md` is the run book
- `package.json` — the repository as a Pi package (`pi install git:github.com/…`); it names
  the same extension as `plugin/package.json`, which a test pins
- `scripts/build_plugin.py` — a self-contained plugin bundle for marketplace installs
- `tests/` — offline tests for the package and the plugin

## Conventions
- The mechanisms (`microskills`, `toolprune`, `loopguard`, `trace`) never import
  `tokeneconomizer.plugin`, and nothing under `tokeneconomizer/` imports `experiments/`; both
  are pinned by `tests/test_plugin_package.py`.
- Standard library only, Python >= 3.10. A hook must start fast and fail open: any exception in
  a hook becomes `{}` and a line in `~/.tokeneconomizer/errors.log`.
- On-disk state names (`injection.json`, `untool.json`, `envelope.json`, event kinds) are a
  compatibility surface; renaming them strands what users have learned.
- Settings keep their earlier names as aliases (`inject`, `untool`, `spiral`, ...; see
  `plugin/config.py`); write new code against the current names.
- No run outputs in the repository: transcripts, rows, streams, figures rendered from runs and
  tables derived from them stay out of git (`.gitignore`). The one exception is the paper's
  headline results in `README.md` (the line under the badges, the Results section, and the
  teaser's closing results, which read `docs/assets/results_overview.py`'s `ROWS`; that script
  also draws `results_overview.*`, which the README no longer shows): quoted from the paper's
  Table 1 and attributed to it. Change them only with the paper, and redraw both figures with
  `python docs/assets/results_overview.py` and `python docs/assets/teaser.py --plex FONTS`
  (its docstring says where to get IBM Plex). The teaser's middle act is a schematic with
  made-up sessions and no numbers.
- The plugin's own text (`plugin/`, its manifests, slash commands and skills, and what the
  hooks print) makes no claims of effect.
- Tests: `python -m pytest tests experiments/tests`. A change to what the plugin learns or
  decides should be checked against recorded sessions, not only the unit tests.
- Every model-backed test goes through the agent's own CLI on a provider you control
  (OpenRouter in development); never hard-code a key.

# TokenEconomizer

A plugin for Claude Code, Codex, the Copilot CLI and Pi that reads finished sessions and changes
what later sessions in the same repository pay for: micro-skills, tool pruning, and a loop guard.
See `README.md` for the overview and the method, `docs/PLUGIN.md` for the design and the verified
agent behavior, and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for how the package fits together.

## Layout
- `tokeneconomizer/` — the one Python package, standard library only
  - `microskills/` — learn repository facts from finished sessions; render the injected block
  - `toolprune/` — unused-tool evidence and the deny-list proposal; Codex capability packages
  - `loopguard/` — the per-call failure-loop guard and its per-repository envelope
  - `trace/` — each agent's session-log format (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Pi, opencode)
  - `plugin/` — the runtime: hook dispatch, per-repository state, settings, the `te` CLI
  - `config.py`, `ledger.py`, `pricing.py`, `domain.py`, `stage.py` — shared by all three
- `plugin/` — the installable plugin directory: manifests per agent, hook files, launchers
  (`scripts/te`, `scripts/te-hook`), slash commands (`slash-commands/`, named in the Claude Code
  and Copilot manifests, since Codex would turn a `commands/` folder into duplicate skills), Codex
  skills (`codex-skills/`, Codex having no plugin slash commands), the Pi extension; `lib/` links
  the package
- `experiments/` — benchmark-only: `te_bench/` (adapters, arms, facade, benchmark-only
  controllers), `te_harness/` (Docker runners), `scripts/`, `workloads/`, its own `tests/`;
  its `README.md` is the run book
- `package.json` — the repository as a Pi package (`pi install git:github.com/…`); it names
  the same extension as `plugin/package.json`, which a test pins
- `scripts/build_plugin.py` — a self-contained plugin bundle for marketplace installs
- `tests/` — offline tests for the package and the plugin

## Conventions
- The mechanisms (`microskills`, `toolprune`, `loopguard`, `trace`) never import
  `tokeneconomizer.plugin`, and nothing under `tokeneconomizer/` imports `experiments/`; both
  are pinned by `tests/test_plugin_package.py`.
- Standard library only, Python >= 3.10. A hook must start fast and fail open: any exception in
  a hook becomes `{}` and a line in `~/.tokeneconomizer/errors.log`.
- On-disk state names (`injection.json`, `untool.json`, `envelope.json`, event kinds) are a
  compatibility surface; renaming them strands what users have learned.
- Settings keep their earlier names as aliases (`inject`, `untool`, `spiral`, ...; see
  `plugin/config.py`); write new code against the current names.
- No run outputs in the repository: transcripts, rows, streams, figures rendered from runs and
  tables derived from them stay out of git (`.gitignore`). The one exception is the paper's
  headline results in `README.md` (the line under the badges, the Results section, and the
  teaser's closing results, which read `docs/assets/results_overview.py`'s `ROWS`; that script
  also draws `results_overview.*`, which the README no longer shows): quoted from the paper's
  Table 1 and attributed to it. Change them only with the paper, and redraw both figures with

  (its docstring says where to get IBM Plex). The teaser's middle act is a schematic with
  made-up sessions and no numbers.
- The plugin's own text (`plugin/`, its manifests, slash commands and skills, and what the
  hooks print) makes no claims of effect.
- Tests: `python -m pytest tests experiments/tests`. A change to what the plugin learns or
  decides should be checked against recorded sessions, not only the unit tests.

# TokenEconomizer R4 — Windows Disposable-Profile Verification

## Goal

Validate the R1–R3 repaired TokenEconomizer candidate on Windows before any production promotion.

**Mode:** Offline verification only. No live Codex model calls, network calls, or production installation.

## Environment

- Windows / PowerShell 7
- Python 3.14
- Codex Desktop and CLI installed
- TokenEconomizer 0.1.0

## Relevant paths

- Original source: `$HOME\CodexTE-Lab\TokenEconomizer`
- R1 evidence: `$HOME\Downloads\REDACTED`
- R2 evidence: `$HOME\Downloads\TokenEconomizer_Repair_R2_20261104_195429_IST`
- R3 evidence: `TokenEconomizer_R3_Offline_Verification_20261104.zip`
- Production project: `E:\TA Projects\EOD Charting Platform`

Resolve paths dynamically where possible. Confirm each file exists. If R3 evidence is not present locally, stop and report the missing prerequisite.

## Phase 1 — Preflight

1. Read applicable project instructions and R1–R3 reports.
2. Verify source revisions and patch checksums.
3. Reconstruct the R3 candidate in a new isolated directory.
4. Verify the installed TokenEconomizer files and configuration without modifying them.
5. Identify all TokenEconomizer state paths and how they are resolved. Confirm the disposable environment cannot redirect writes into the live profile.

## Phase 2 — Windows integration tests

Use disposable directories under `$HOME\Downloads` for test repositories, configuration, ledger, and synthetic Codex rollouts.

Test:

- SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, and SessionEnd.
- Correct Windows path handling.
- Native PowerShell and Python hook invocation.
- Reasoning-token accounting without double-counting.
- Archived rollout recovery.
- Missing, invalid, duplicate, and overlapping session records.
- Repeated and interrupted hook calls.
- Ledger idempotency.
- Missing-index recovery.
- Correct handling of incomplete folds.
- No unauthorized pruning or configuration changes.
- No writes outside the explicitly approved disposable directories.

Do not invoke the real Codex CLI/Desktop host during R4. Test hook entry points with synthetic events. Set isolation variables only in child processes, never persist changes to the user's environment.

## Phase 3 — Regression verification

Run the relevant offline regression tests.

Do not add dependencies without approval. Preserve existing behavior. Avoid excessive terminal output and repeated investigations.

## Phase 4 — Evidence

Create a sanitized R4 evidence package under `$HOME\Downloads` containing:

- Source and patch integrity checks.
- Hook execution results.
- Regression-test results.
- Disposable-profile isolation verification.
- File-write inventory.
- Remaining risks and limitations.

# TokenEconomizer

A plugin for Claude Code, Codex, the Copilot CLI and Pi that reads finished sessions and changes
what later sessions in the same repository pay for: micro-skills, tool pruning, and a loop guard.
See `README.md` for the overview and the method, `docs/PLUGIN.md` for the design and the verified
agent behavior, and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for how the package fits together.

## Layout
- `tokeneconomizer/` — the one Python package, standard library only
  - `microskills/` — learn repository facts from finished sessions; render the injected block
  - `toolprune/` — unused-tool evidence and the deny-list proposal; Codex capability packages
  - `loopguard/` — the per-call failure-loop guard and its per-repository envelope
  - `trace/` — each agent's session-log format (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Pi, opencode)
  - `plugin/` — the runtime: hook dispatch, per-repository state, settings, the `te` CLI
  - `config.py`, `ledger.py`, `pricing.py`, `domain.py`, `stage.py` — shared by all three
- `plugin/` — the installable plugin directory: manifests per agent, hook files, launchers
  (`scripts/te`, `scripts/te-hook`), slash commands (`slash-commands/`, named in the Claude Code
  and Copilot manifests, since Codex would turn a `commands/` folder into duplicate skills), Codex
  skills (`codex-skills/`, Codex having no plugin slash commands), the Pi extension; `lib/` links
  the package
- `experiments/` — benchmark-only: `te_bench/` (adapters, arms, facade, benchmark-only
  controllers), `te_harness/` (Docker runners), `scripts/`, `workloads/`, its own `tests/`;
  its `README.md` is the run book
- `package.json` — the repository as a Pi package (`pi install git:github.com/…`); it names
  the same extension as `plugin/package.json`, which a test pins
- `scripts/build_plugin.py` — a self-contained plugin bundle for marketplace installs
- `tests/` — offline tests for the package and the plugin

## Conventions
- The mechanisms (`microskills`, `toolprune`, `loopguard`, `trace`) never import
  `tokeneconomizer.plugin`, and nothing under `tokeneconomizer/` imports `experiments/`; both
  are pinned by `tests/test_plugin_package.py`.
- Standard library only, Python >= 3.10. A hook must start fast and fail open: any exception in
  a hook becomes `{}` and a line in `~/.tokeneconomizer/errors.log`.
- On-disk state names (`injection.json`, `untool.json`, `envelope.json`, event kinds) are a
  compatibility surface; renaming them strands what users have learned.
- Settings keep their earlier names as aliases (`inject`, `untool`, `spiral`, ...; see
  `plugin/config.py`); write new code against the current names.
- No run outputs in the repository: transcripts, rows, streams, figures rendered from runs and
  tables derived from them stay out of git (`.gitignore`). The one exception is the paper's
  headline results in `README.md` (the line under the badges, the Results section, and the
  teaser's closing results, which read `docs/assets/results_overview.py`'s `ROWS`; that script
  also draws `results_overview.*`, which the README no longer shows): quoted from the paper's
  Table 1 and attributed to it. Change them only with the paper, and redraw both figures with
  `python docs/assets/results_overview.py` and `python docs/assets/teaser.py --plex FONTS`
  (its docstring says where to get IBM Plex). The teaser's middle act is a schematic with
  made-up sessions and no numbers.
- The plugin's own text (`plugin/`, its manifests, slash commands and skills, and what the
  hooks print) makes no claims of effect.
- Tests: `python -m pytest tests experiments/tests`. A change to what the plugin learns or
  decides should be checked against recorded sessions, not only the unit tests.
- Every model-backed test goes through the agent's own CLI on a provider you control
  (OpenRouter in development); never hard-code a key.

# TokenEconomizer 0.1.0 accounting repair R2

4 November 2026 IST · Windows · isolated R1 candidate · base revision `85a8247bf4fc276a6f681446c359d7ca021b83b9`

## Review findings

1. **Recoverable stale paths.** R1 stopped at the first unusable path. The new tests reproduced the failure with both a missing file and malformed text before a readable rollout. R2 examines all candidates and can use a valid rollout when a path is missing, has invalid text before a recognizable rollout record, or fails identity checks. The fold uses the selected readable rollout for its trace.
2. **Incomplete folds are final.** R2 writes `usage_finality: permanent_incomplete` and a diagnostic status for unpriced Codex folds. Under the existing fold lock, it also checks the ledger before rerunning a session whose fold index entry is absent. A complete existing row prevents a second append and mechanism replay. A regression removes the synthetic index after an incomplete fold, then supplies a valid transcript and verifies the original row remains the only row. The repair neither backfills nor edits historical ledgers.
3. **Identity and provenance.** Canonical Codex UUIDs must match the rollout's initial session metadata. When both ID fields exist, both must agree. The metadata's absolute working directory must resolve to the pinned checkout root or the recorded start directory. The tests cover a misleading filename with a wrong ID, a foreign checkout, and missing working-directory metadata. Unverified paths cannot contribute tokens or become the chosen mechanism trace. Legacy non-UUID explicit paths remain single-path inputs and are not discovered or combined by the fold.

# TokenEconomizer R3 — Isolated Hook Lifecycle Verification

**Status: OFFLINE SYNTHETIC PASS / PRODUCTION PROMOTION HOLD**

Date: 2026-11-04. Verification executed on an isolated Linux container, **not** on the user's Windows Codex Desktop or Codex CLI installation.

## Source integrity

- Source basis: the candidate bundled inside the supplied R1 archive, derived from reported base revision `85a8247bf4fc276a6f681446c359d7ca021b83b9` (revision not independently checked against Git metadata because the ZIP has none).
- R1 patch SHA-256 matches report: `85F5960D46D30368CECD08ADB822E5C59E5021D5F5219BFB74AD9B173798E75C`.
- R2 incremental patch SHA-256 matches report: `354724A33D0D5088DA5F66A6272F70544BB1A788C39E1B018A7C52125EB81C25`.
- R2 applied to the isolated R1 candidate after normalizing mixed CRLF/LF in three affected files; `git apply --check` and reverse check pass.
- No source file from the user's production project, original source checkout or installed plugin was mounted or modified.

## Independent test results

- **270 passed, 1 skipped, 1 deselected** across accounting, trace, ledger, live core, and live hooks. The skipped test is Windows-only (case-insensitive paths). The deselected test can launch child processes. No Codex CLI integration module run.
- **48 synthetic lifecycle checks passed**, executing the actual `plugin/scripts/te_bootstrap.py hook --host codex` entrypoint in separate Python invocations.
- Five tested hook types: `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`.
- Four synthetic session ledger rows, all checked for expected state and idempotency.

## Behavioral checks

- Archived valid rollout recovered after a malformed active transcript path.
- Output included reasoning exactly once; sample output **20**, reasoning subset **7**, weighted effective result **162** under the candidate's fallback curve.
- Repeated `SessionEnd` and missing `folded.json` index did not duplicate ledger rows.
- A missing rollout yielded a permanently incomplete, unpriced ledger record; later evidence was not silently backfilled.
- A foreign checkout rollout was ignored in favor of a valid archive candidate.
- Conflicting overlapping rollout candidates remained unpriced.
- No Codex `.codex/config.toml` was created, and the synthetic repository's file checksums were unchanged.
- Hook processes were supplied a fresh `HOME`, `TOKENECONOMIZER_HOME`, and `CODEX_HOME`; sidecall-prone mechanisms were disabled and child-process/network calls were blocked inside each hook process.

## Scope and limitations

1. This is a **synthetic Python-entrypoint test**, not proof that Codex Desktop or Codex CLI on Windows delivered the actual native hook payloads or lifecycle ordering.
2. LoopGuard was disabled in integration scenarios to prevent any model-backed sidecalls. It remains covered by the existing offline test suite, not an R3 live trial.
3. Only the relevant five offline test modules were run. This is not the full repository test suite.
4. Historical inaccessible rollouts remain inaccessible. R2's permanent-incomplete policy does not reconcile historical missing usage automatically.
5. No controlled A/B benchmark was run; **token savings and 5-hour allowance savings are not verified**.
6. The initial R2 patch required line-ending normalization when applied to the archived R1 tree. Packaging should standardize this before a Windows promotion.
7. A portable Linux sandbox cannot verify registry, shell escaping, trust approvals, desktop host integration, or real Windows path behavior.

## Decision

**R3 offline verification PASS. Promotion HOLD.** No evidence in this test justifies replacing the active TokenEconomizer 0.1.0 plugin.

Next: Run the same sealed candidate under a disposable **Windows** `CODEX_HOME`/`TOKENECONOMIZER_HOME` profile, with local synthetic hook invocation, blocked external calls, no production project access and no automatic promotion. 4 November 2026 IST · PowerShell 7.6.5 · Python 3.14.8

## Integrity and preflight

The original source was clean at \`85a8247bf4fc276a6f681446c359d7ca021b83b9\`. R3 is evidence for the R1 + R2 source, with no additional source patch. A new local clone without object hardlinks was reconstructed from that revision. Both patches passed forward apply checks. Git emitted an R1 intermediate blank-line warning. | Artifact | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| R1 patch | \`85F5960D46D30368CECD08ADB822E5C59E5021D5F5219BFB74AD9B173798E75C\` |
| R2 patch, including the copy inside R3 | \`354724A33D0D5088DA5F66A6272F70544BB1A788C39E1B018A7C52125EB81C25\` |
| Local R3 ZIP | \`4EFE33A7DEFCF44A42AE9C476EE3326F502D96AC13E6646CB9D1E46C4E022602\` |

The installed manifest reported 0.1.0. Read-only checks found global enablement, shadow false, global pruning auto, and the EOD repository override propose. Installed manifest, hook, bootstrap, and core pointer were fingerprinted. The installed hook and bootstrap were never invoked. Live TokenEconomizer state, Codex configuration, and production project were outside the integration profiles.

## Windows results

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| Direct Python bootstrap | PASS, 57 checks and five session rows |
| Native PowerShell manifest command | PASS, 57 checks and five session rows |
| Direct Python with LoopGuard active | PASS, 58 checks and five session rows |
| Native PowerShell with LoopGuard active and shell telemetry and update checks disabled | PASS, 58 checks and five session rows |
| Offline accounting, trace, ledger, live core, and live hook regressions | PASS, 271 passed, one deselected |

All four integration runs delivered synthetic SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop and SessionEnd through the actual candidate bootstrap. The native runs executed the manifest's exact \`commandWindows\` through PowerShell. Profiles used Windows paths containing spaces and a non-ASCII character. The active LoopGuard runs verified that PostToolUse and Stop wrote a one-call turn record without a judge. A resumed session was tested by omitting Stop and SessionEnd before a second SessionStart. No process was forcibly killed.

Both transports recovered an archived rollout after malformed active text, counted mirrored usage once, rejected foreign checkout metadata and left overlapping segments unpriced. The sample retained output 20 and reasoning 7 with weighted result 162. Repeated SessionEnd and simulated fold-index loss left one row. Missing usage remained permanently incomplete when later evidence appeared. Synthetic repo files were unchanged and no Codex project settings file or pruning was applied. The regression run deselected the local probe launcher fixture and excluded real Codex integration modules. Initial regression setup could not resolve the already-installed pytest after changing USERPROFILE. Later attempts blocked the Windows null-device alias before collection. The passing run added the existing dependency path and allowed the exact null-device alias.

## Isolation and writes

Child-only environment variables routed the state root, global and repo settings, launcher, pin and repo index, session snapshots, fold index, ledger, locks, mechanism files, and error logs through disposable \`TOKENECONOMIZER_HOME\`. \`CODEX_HOME\` isolated active and archived rollouts and any global Codex lookup. Working-directory settings resolved inside the synthetic repo. HOME, USERPROFILE, home-drive/path, AppData, TEMP and TMP were set to disposable locations. TE_CORE_PATH selected the fresh candidate. The final native run scrubbed inherited agent overrides and disabled shell telemetry and update checking. Hook PATH excluded Codex, and folding ran inline under the test flag.

All 72 hook Python processes armed the audit guard. The guard blocked network and subprocess APIs and rejected resolved writes outside each profile. Negative controls independently blocked an out-of-root write, a socket connect, and a process launch before execution. The passing hook runs recorded zero guard violations. The regression guard allowed local Git fixture operations and the Windows null device. The evidence contains a write-event inventory and persistent synthetic hook file inventory. Harness and guard logs were written under this R4 directory. No Codex host, paid-model call, dependency install, live configuration change or promotion occurred.

The guard observes Python-level activity. It does not provide OS-wide tracing of PowerShell, Git, or other native code. The initial native run did not explicitly opt out of PowerShell telemetry. The final opt-out run is the basis of the native verification. The offline tests validate inline folding and simulated interruption. Detached folding, Codex trust prompts, actual Desktop and CLI payload delivery, and crash timing remain unverified.

- **STATUS** — Windows offline verification **PASS**. Production promotion **HOLD**.
- **RISKS** — Real-host event delivery, trust and detached workers still need verification. Historical incomplete rows still require a separately reviewed reconciliation. No token-savings or subscription impact was measured.
- **FILES CHANGED** — Fresh candidate and synthetic fixtures, harnesses, and evidence under the R4 Downloads folder only. The original checkout, installed plugin, production project, and existing ledgers were untouched by the verification.
- **NEXT STEPS** — In R5, separately authorize real-host tests in a disposable Windows profile. Verify Desktop and CLI trust, event delivery, detached fold completion, interruption recovery, and rollback before any promotion decision.

# TokenEconomizer

A plugin for Claude Code, Codex, the Copilot CLI and Pi that reads finished sessions and changes
what later sessions in the same repository pay for: micro-skills, tool pruning, and a loop guard.
See `README.md` for the overview and the method, `docs/PLUGIN.md` for the design and the verified
agent behavior, and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for how the package fits together.

## Layout
- `tokeneconomizer/` — the one Python package, standard library only
  - `microskills/` — learn repository facts from finished sessions; render the injected block
  - `toolprune/` — unused-tool evidence and the deny-list proposal; Codex capability packages
  - `loopguard/` — the per-call failure-loop guard and its per-repository envelope
  - `trace/` — each agent's session-log format (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Pi, opencode)
  - `plugin/` — the runtime: hook dispatch, per-repository state, settings, the `te` CLI
  - `config.py`, `ledger.py`, `pricing.py`, `domain.py`, `stage.py` — shared by all three
- `plugin/` — the installable plugin directory: manifests per agent, hook files, launchers
  (`scripts/te`, `scripts/te-hook`), slash commands (`slash-commands/`, named in the Claude Code
  and Copilot manifests, since Codex would turn a `commands/` folder into duplicate skills), Codex
  skills (`codex-skills/`, Codex having no plugin slash commands), the Pi extension; `lib/` links
  the package
- `experiments/` — benchmark-only: `te_bench/` (adapters, arms, facade, benchmark-only
  controllers), `te_harness/` (Docker runners), `scripts/`, `workloads/`, its own `tests/`;
  its `README.md` is the run book
- `package.json` — the repository as a Pi package (`pi install git:github.com/…`); it names
  the same extension as `plugin/package.json`, which a test pins
- `scripts/build_plugin.py` — a self-contained plugin bundle for marketplace installs
- `tests/` — offline tests for the package and the plugin

## Conventions
- The mechanisms (`microskills`, `toolprune`, `loopguard`, `trace`) never import
  `tokeneconomizer.plugin`, and nothing under `tokeneconomizer/` imports `experiments/`; both
  are pinned by `tests/test_plugin_package.py`.
- Standard library only, Python >= 3.10. A hook must start fast and fail open: any exception in
  a hook becomes `{}` and a line in `~/.tokeneconomizer/errors.log`.
- On-disk state names (`injection.json`, `untool.json`, `envelope.json`, event kinds) are a
  compatibility surface; renaming them strands what users have learned.
- Settings keep their earlier names as aliases (`inject`, `untool`, `spiral`, ...; see
  `plugin/config.py`); write new code against the current names.
- No run outputs in the repository: transcripts, rows, streams, figures rendered from runs and
  tables derived from them stay out of git (`.gitignore`). The one exception is the paper's
  headline results in `README.md` (the line under the badges, the Results section, and the
  teaser's closing results, which read `docs/assets/results_overview.py`'s `ROWS`; that script
  also draws `results_overview.*`, which the README no longer shows): quoted from the paper's
  Table 1 and attributed to it. Change them only with the paper, and redraw both figures with
  `python docs/assets/results_overview.py` and `python docs/assets/teaser.py --plex FONTS`
  (its docstring says where to get IBM Plex). The teaser's middle act is a schematic with
  made-up sessions and no numbers.
- The plugin's own text (`plugin/`, its manifests, slash commands and skills, and what the
  hooks print) makes no claims of effect.
- Tests: `python -m pytest tests experiments/tests`. A change to what the plugin learns or
  decides should be checked against recorded sessions, not only the unit tests.
- Every model-backed test goes through the agent's own CLI on a provider you control
  (OpenRouter in development); never hard-code a key.

Both transports recovered an archived rollout after malformed active text, counted mirrored usage once, rejected foreign checkout metadata and left overlapping segments unpriced. The sample retained output 20 and reasoning 7 with weighted result 162. Repeated SessionEnd and simulated fold-index loss left one row. Missing usage remained permanently incomplete when later evidence appeared. Synthetic repo files were unchanged and no Codex project settings file or pruning was applied. The regression run deselected the local probe launcher fixture and excluded real Codex integration modules. Initial regression setup could not resolve the already-installed pytest after changing USERPROFILE. Later attempts blocked the Windows null-device alias before collection. The passing run added the existing dependency path and allowed the exact null-device alias.

## Isolation and writes

Child-only environment variables routed the state root, global and repo settings, launcher, pin and repo index, session snapshots, fold index, ledger, locks, mechanism files, and error logs through disposable `TOKENECONOMIZER_HOME`. `CODEX_HOME` isolated active and archived rollouts and any global Codex lookup. Working-directory settings resolved inside the synthetic repo. HOME, USERPROFILE, home-drive/path, AppData, TEMP and TMP were set to disposable locations. TE_CORE_PATH selected the fresh candidate. The final native run scrubbed inherited agent overrides and disabled shell telemetry and update checking. Hook PATH excluded Codex, and folding ran inline under the test flag.

All 72 hook Python processes armed the audit guard. The guard blocked network and subprocess APIs and rejected resolved writes outside each profile. Negative controls independently blocked an out-of-root write, a socket connect, and a process launch before execution. The passing hook runs recorded zero guard violations. The regression guard allowed local Git fixture operations and the Windows null device. The evidence contains a write-event inventory and persistent synthetic hook file inventory. Harness and guard logs were written under this R4 directory. No Codex host, paid-model call, dependency install, live configuration change or promotion occurred.

The guard observes Python-level activity. It does not provide OS-wide tracing of PowerShell, Git, or other native code. The initial native run did not explicitly opt out of PowerShell telemetry. The final opt-out run is the basis of the native verification. The offline tests validate inline folding and simulated interruption. Detached folding, Codex trust prompts, actual Desktop and CLI payload delivery, and crash timing remain unverified.

- **STATUS** — Windows offline verification **PASS**. Production promotion **HOLD**.
- **RISKS** — Real-host event delivery, trust and detached workers still need verification. Historical incomplete rows still require a separately reviewed reconciliation. No token-savings or subscription impact was measured.
- **FILES CHANGED** — Fresh candidate and synthetic fixtures, harnesses, and evidence under the R4 Downloads folder only. The original checkout, installed plugin, production project, and existing ledgers were untouched by the verification.
- **NEXT STEPS** — In R5, separately authorize real-host tests in a disposable Windows profile. Verify Desktop and CLI trust, event delivery, detached fold completion, interruption recovery, and rollback before any promotion decision.

Installing or enabling a plugin doesn’t automatically trust its hooks. Plugin-bundled hooks are non-managed hooks, so Codex skips them until the user reviews and trusts the current hook definition.

### Enable or disable a plugin for a repo

The repo marketplace at `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` makes plugins discoverable. Use the repo’s `.codex/config.toml` to control whether a local-marketplace plugin is enabled for that project:
    
    `[plugins."my-plugin@local-repo"]
    enabled = true`

The quoted key uses `plugin-name@marketplace-name`: `my-plugin` is the plugin entry’s name, and `local-repo` is the marketplace’s top-level `name`. Set `enabled = false` to disable the plugin for the project without uninstalling it. During marketplace refresh, Codex can install or refresh files for configured plugins, even when `enabled = false`. Connected services still require authentication.

Codex loads project `.codex/config.toml` only for trusted projects. Project settings override user, cloud-managed, and system defaults, subject to enforced requirements. See Configuration precedence.

These settings apply to local-marketplace plugins in supported local clients, including Codex CLI and Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app. They don’t change workspace installation policies for plugins imported through Admin > Plugins. Those plugins use their workspace-managed enabled state, even when their source is a GitHub repository. See Import and sync plugins from GitHub.

#### Configure installed server policy

After installation, users can enable or disable a bundled MCP server and tune tool approval policy from their Codex config without editing the plugin. Use `plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>` for plugin-scoped MCP server policy:
    
    `[plugins."my-plugin".mcp_servers.docs]
    enabled = true
    default_tools_approval_mode = "prompt"
    enabled_tools = ["search"]
    
    [plugins."my-plugin".mcp_servers.docs.tools.search]
    approval_mode = "approve"`

When your plugin is enabled, the Codex runtime can load lifecycle hooks from your plugin alongside user, project, and managed hooks. This includes ChatGPT Work and Codex. Hook scripts must exist in the execution environment; installing a plugin on the web doesn’t deploy them. Enterprise admins can deploy required scripts through mobile device management (MDM).

Installing or enabling a plugin doesn’t automatically trust its hooks. Plugin-bundled hooks are non-managed hooks, so Codex skips them until the user reviews and trusts the current hook definition.

Codex discovers `hooks/hooks.json` by default when the selected OpenAI extension or compatibility manifest doesn’t define `hooks`:
    
    `{
      "hooks": {
        "SessionStart": [
          {
            "hooks": [
              {
                "type": "command",
                "command": "python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/session_start.py",
                "statusMessage": "Loading plugin context"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }`

To override that default, define `hooks` inside `extensions.com.openai` in root `plugin.json`. The field can be a single path, an array of paths, an inline hooks object, or an array of inline hooks objects. An explicit value replaces default-file discovery; it doesn’t add to `hooks/hooks.json`.
    
    `{
      "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json",
      "name": "repo-policy",
      "extensions": {
        "com.openai": {
          "hooks": ["./hooks/session.json", "./hooks/tools.json"]
        }
      }
    }`

Legacy packages can declare `hooks` directly in `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`.

Hook paths start with `./`, resolve relative to the plugin root, and stay inside the plugin root.

Plugin hook commands receive the Codex-specific environment variables `PLUGIN_ROOT` and `PLUGIN_DATA`. `PLUGIN_ROOT` points to the installed plugin root, and `PLUGIN_DATA` points to the plugin’s writable data directory. Codex also sets `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` for compatibility with existing plugin hooks.

Plugin hooks use the same event schema as regular hooks. See Hooks on Learn for supported events, inputs, outputs, trust review, and current limitations.

L3549: 
L3550: Check for and apply a Codex CLI update when the installed release supports self-update. Debug builds print a message telling you to install a release build instead.
L3551: ## Flag combinations and safety tips
L3552: 
L3553:   * Use `--sandbox workspace-write` for unattended local work that can stay inside the workspace, and avoid `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` unless you are inside a dedicated sandbox VM.
L3554:   * When you need to grant Codex write access to more directories, prefer `--add-dir` rather than forcing `--sandbox danger-full-access`.
L3555:   * Pair `--json` with `--output-last-message` in CI to capture machine-readable progress and a final natural-language summary.
L3556: ## Interactive shortcuts
L3557:   * Type `@` to search for a file in the workspace and add its path to the prompt.
L3558:   * Press `Up` or `Down` to restore draft history.
L3559:   * Press `Ctrl`+`R` to search prompt history, then press `Enter` to use a match or `Escape` to cancel.
L3560:   * Press `Ctrl`+` O ` to copy the latest completed response. Run `/copy` to choose what to copy.
L3561:   * Prefix a line with `!` to run a local shell command under the current approval and sandbox settings.
L3562:   * Press `Tab` while Codex is working to queue a follow-up prompt, slash command, or shell command for the next turn.
L3563:   * Press `Enter` while Codex is working to inject new instructions into the current turn.
L3564:   * Press `Escape` twice with an empty composer to edit the previous user message and fork the chat from that point.
L3565:   * Press `Ctrl`+`C` or run `/exit` to close the session.

const report=`# TokenEconomizer R5A real-host isolation preflight

4 November 2026 IST · Windows · preview only

## Results

- **PASS — Candidate integrity.** R4 ZIP passed its archive check and its report matched the extracted report. The original checkout was clean. Both checkouts resolve to \`85a8247bf4fc276a6f681446c359d7ca021b83b9\`. Reapplying the hash-verified R1 and R2 patches to a temporary Git index reproduced the candidate exactly, including its added regression file. The candidate is TokenEconomizer 0.1.0. Its legacy local marketplace is \`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json\`. Its Codex manifest points to \`plugin/hooks/codex-hooks.json\`, with five Windows hook commands.
- **PASS — Candidate path resolution with boundaries.** The first child Python probe found a real escape from the intended fixture. An unversioned Downloads fixture inherited the ancestor home checkout, which resolved the project settings target to the real user's \`.codex/config.toml\`. No settings write or hook ran. A synthetic Git root and explicit \`GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES\` corrected the resolution. The revised child resolved both state homes, repository settings, launcher, temporary directory and profile home inside the preview. Pruning, micro-skills and repo-map were off. LoopGuard was configured for nudge and the inline-fold override was absent.
- **HOLD — Exclusive native host isolation.** R4 proved synthetic entry-point behavior. R5A proves static wiring and candidate path resolution. It does not establish the installed CLI's effective configuration, plugin loader, trust store, credential selection or write paths at runtime. No Codex executable or wrapper was invoked. The source test suite shows the legacy marketplace commands and a loopback fixture, but its lifecycle integration test bypasses hook trust. It cannot serve as the R5B trust check.

## Path and isolation map

| Owner | Disposable routing and controls |
|---|---|
| Codex CLI | Explicit absolute native binary inside the test environment. Use an allowlisted child environment, dedicated \`CODEX_HOME\`, fixture working directory, and no production project or parent workspace. Stage only the candidate's local marketplace. Inspect the resulting marketplace source, enablement and cache before trusting hooks. |
| Codex state | Profile \`config.toml\`, \`hooks.json\` if any, trust state, plugin discovery/cache/data, active and archived sessions, session index, SQLite databases, logs, history, temp and updates. Set absolute SQLite and log roots inside the test profile. Check for inherited home-level \`.agents\`, project config, system/managed hooks, requirements and any shared endpoints. |
| Credentials | Use a fresh Windows principal with an empty credential store and profile. Set CLI and MCP credential stores to file for the test. Do not copy \`auth.json\`, login, enable connectors, or pass host keys, access tokens, identity-token files, proxies or agent sockets. The live auth file was observed by existence only. File-backed stores and scrubbed variables address intended routes, while Windows Credential Manager, SSO and enforced managed policy remain outside a same-user path preview. |
| TokenEconomizer | Explicit \`TOKENECONOMIZER_HOME\` routes global config, repository config, pins, repo index, launcher and per-repo Codex state, including locks, sessions, ledger, fold index, event logs, mechanism state and error logs. \`CODEX_HOME\` routes transcript discovery and global Codex lookups. \`TE_CORE_PATH\` selects the sealed guest copy. Project pruning targets the resolved checkout's \`.codex/config.toml\`; keep pruning off. |
| Windows children | Set HOME, USERPROFILE, HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA, TEMP and TMP only for the guest test process. Disable shell telemetry and update checks. The fold worker inherits the hook environment. The WMI fallback can run outside the launching job and writes a temporary command/environment specification beside the fold log. Keep credentials out of that environment, track the WMI-launched worker separately and keep all test state on guest storage. |

System, managed and lower-layer hooks can coexist with profile settings. A profile directory is a routing choice, not a filesystem or network boundary. R5B requires a disposable Windows VM or equivalent enforced boundary, no writable host drive mappings, no production credentials, blocked external egress and guest-local loopback. Guest-wide policy and Windows sandbox provisioning are outside this preview. Stop if policy forces a shared store, connector, or endpoint. Codex Desktop remains outside the CLI test scope. [Configuration reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference) · [Plugin packaging and trust](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins) · [Hook review](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks)

## R5B runbook — unexecuted, separate authorization required

1. In a fresh offline Windows guest, copy the sealed candidate and native CLI as read-only inputs, with no host drive mappings during execution. Use a standard guest user. Create an isolated root and a new repository with \`git -C $Repo init -q\`. Set all environment paths above in a dedicated child PowerShell. Point \`GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES\` to the test root, disable Git system/global config for the fixture, and remove inherited \`TE_*\`, \`CODEX_*\`, \`OPENAI_*\`, auth, provider and proxy settings before setting the allowlist. Set \`TE_TOOLPRUNE=off\`, \`TE_MICROSKILLS=off\`, \`TE_REPOMAP=off\`, \`TE_LOOPGUARD=nudge\`, \`TE_SHADOW=false\`. Leave \`TE_FOLD_SYNC\` unset. Capture guest filesystem/process tracing before launching Codex, including WMI descendants and network attempts. Retain only path and status evidence. If guest isolation or tracing is unavailable, stop.
2. Build and inspect a bounded loopback Responses fixture from the candidate's \`tests/test_codex_cli.py\` fixture before CLI launch. Extend it to return one deterministic read-only command request against the fixture, then a final response. Provide a second scenario that pauses the response long enough to interrupt. Cap the fixture at six POSTs total, zero retries and no external listeners. Set \`model = "te-test-model"\`, \`model_provider = "te_test"\`, and configure \`[model_providers.te_test]\` with the fixture's explicit \`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1\`, \`wire_api = "responses"\`, \`supports_websockets = false\`, and zero request/stream retries. Use no real auth. Stop if the pinned build requires external sign-in or the reviewed fixture is unavailable. The fixture extension is preparation for R5B, not a runnable artifact of this preview.
3. With \`$CodexExe\` bound to the verified guest binary, run \`& $CodexExe --version\`, then from the fixture directory \`& $CodexExe plugin marketplace add $Candidate\` and \`& $CodexExe plugin add 'tokeneconomizer@tokeneconomizer'\`. Expect successful exit and a marketplace source/cache confined to guest paths. Stop on unknown flags, compatibility errors, sandbox provisioning prompts, extra hooks/plugins, writes outside the allowed guest roots, or any non-loopback connection attempt. Do not substitute a remote marketplace or modify system requirements.
4. From the fixture directory run \`& $CodexExe --sandbox read-only --ask-for-approval never\`. Inspect \`/hooks\`. Confirm the candidate is the only non-managed hook source, and document its initial trust status without submitting a prompt. Review and trust only the five expected candidate definitions. Do not use the trust bypass. Submit the synthetic read-only task once, expect the fixture's final reply, then \`/exit\`. Inspect \`Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $env:TOKENECONOMIZER_HOME -Recurse -Filter ledger.jsonl\`. Within 60 seconds expect one row for the completed session, one priced set of usage fields, a Stop turn with one tool call and a detached fold trace. Cross-check native hook delivery and the raw reasoning subset against the rollout. If the provider never emits a supported tool event, mark PostToolUse unverified and stop.
5. Launch the same command once more against the delayed scenario. Interrupt with Ctrl+C while the fixture is waiting. Record whether SessionEnd ran. If absent, close the test process, age only that synthetic rollout past the candidate's 600-second quiet threshold, then launch one final fixture session to exercise SessionStart recovery. Check \`fold.log\`, the fold index and ledger by session ID. After all workers close, remove only the synthetic fold-index entry for the completed session and run one candidate maintenance fold in the same child environment with \`& $PythonExe -B -m tokeneconomizer.plugin.cli fold --session $SessionId --host codex --cwd $Repo\` and guest \`PYTHONPATH\` bound to the sealed candidate. Expect the index to be rebuilt and one ledger row for that ID. Keep this maintenance test separate from real SessionEnd evidence. Stop on duplicates, timeout, active workers after the window, or unexpected state.
6. Rollback is guest-only. Close the fixture and CLI, then wait up to 60 seconds for identified detached workers, including any WMI-started workers. Preserve sanitized results and revert the guest snapshot or discard the exact test profile after confirming no writer remains. Never use a broad process kill, log out of the host, or uninstall the production plugin.

The operator must review the loopback fixture, guest boundary and actual binary options before the authorized launch. Exact native behavior on the installed Windows build remains the open gate.

- **STATUS** — Candidate integrity and bounded Python path preview **PASS**. Native isolation and R5B execution **HOLD**.
- **RISKS** — Same-user profile variables do not isolate OS credentials, managed configuration, native workers or all writes. The ancestor checkout escape was reproduced and corrected for the preview.
- **FILES CHANGED** — This report, sanitized integrity/configuration records and a synthetic path-probe fixture under the R5A Downloads directory. No changes to R4, the installed plugin, live Codex configuration, existing ledgers or EOD.
- **NEXT STEPS** — Separately authorize R5B only after reviewing the disposable guest boundary and the loopback fixture. No R5B commands were run.
`;
await eval(load("r5run"))(`@'\n${report}\n'@ | Set-Content -LiteralPath report.md -Encoding utf8NoBOM; Get-ChildItem -File | Select-Object Name,Length`)
